acceptance_criteria.criterion: In legacy mode (null config), resolveStoreForWrite() delegates to resolveLedgerRoot() and isMultiStoreMode() returns false
With a repo registered in the first store, resolveStoreForWrite() returns the first store's path
With a repo registered in the second store only, resolveStoreForWrite() returns the second store's path
With the same repo registered in both stores, resolveStoreForWrite() returns the first store's path (store-order priority)
With an unregistered repo in multi-store mode, resolveStoreForWrite() throws an error containing "not registered in any store"
On construction, each configured store path that does not exist on disk is created via mkdirSync with { recursive: true }

comments.note: store-router.ts: The stores array is re-iterated in resolveStoreForRepo() on every call — for the expected store counts (1–10 typically) this is fine, but if store counts grow large, caching a Map<repoName, storeRef> after the first lookup would avoid repeated registry I/O.

store-registry.ts: expandStorePath() is a utility that conceptually belongs in a path-utils module rather than the store-registry I/O module; it is already imported in store-router.ts directly from store-registry.js which is slightly surprising for consumers — a future refactor could extract it to utils/path-utils.ts.
